mainTopic: רבי שמעון's view of מוקצה and of unintended acts (דבר שאין מתכוין), shown through the lamp, the בכור, and vows
overview: This amud opens at the end of a story. רב אויא gives his last answer to רבא: a ברייתא says jewelry may be moved in a courtyard on שבת, and עולא explains that this is because it has the status of a כלי. The same reason works for רב אויא's case, and רב נחמן בר יצחק thanks God that רבא did not embarrass him. Then אביי raises a contradiction before רבה. רבי שמעון allows leftover lamp oil, which suggests he does not hold of מוקצה. Yet he forbids a בכור whose blemish was not noticeable before יום טוב. רבה answers that a person expects his lamp to go out, but nobody counts on a blemish, a permanent one, and a חכם willing to examine it. Two challenges from vows are answered: a wife's vow always depends on her husband, and three ordinary people can release a vow if no חכם will. Next, אביי asks רב יוסף why רבי שמעון forbids moving a burning lamp, since he permits unintended acts like dragging furniture. The first answer splits Torah-level and rabbinic results. רבא knocks that answer down with the case of clothing merchants, and the amud ends just as רבא begins a new explanation, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא about bracelets, nose-rings and rings
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא quotes a ברייתא: jewelry like bracelets, nose-rings and rings may be moved in a courtyard on שבת, just like any other כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bracelets, nose-rings and rings are like all the vessels that may be moved in the courtyard.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אויא brings a ברייתא as proof for his answer to רבא. The ברייתא says jewelry counts like any normal כלי for moving in a courtyard on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You may not go out into the street wearing some of this jewelry on שבת. Even so, the ברייתא says they are not forbidden to move in the courtyard. So being restricted in one way does not make an item מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: bracelets
nose-rings
rings
vessels that may be moved in a courtyard on שבת

phrases.english: Bracelets, nose-rings, and rings,
they are like all the vessels
that may be moved in the courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב אויא's answer to רבא from before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That an item with the status of a כלי may be moved on שבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about jewelry in the courtyard

steps.title: עולא explains why the jewelry may be moved
steps.stepSummary: עולא gives the reason: the jewelry may be moved because it has the status of a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And עולא said: What is the reason? Because the status of a vessel applies to them.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא explains the reason behind the ברייתא. The jewelry may be moved because it counts as a כלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא only gave the rule. עולא adds the principle behind it: having the status of a כלי is enough to allow moving an item. This principle is the part רב אויא really needs.

keyTerms.meaning: what is the reason?
since, because
the status of a vessel

phrases.english: And Ulla said: What is the reason?
Since the status of a vessel applies to them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the ברייתא in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Having the status of a כלי allows an item to be moved on שבת.

steps.title: The same reason works for our case
steps.stepSummary: רב אויא uses עולא's reason for the case he was asked about: it too has the status of a כלי, so it may be moved.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, since the status of a vessel applies to them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אויא now finishes his answer to רבא. The case they were discussing works the same way as the jewelry, because it also has the status of a כלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is where the proof pays off. עולא's general reason from the jewelry case is carried over to the item in רבא's question. That item may be moved on שבת for the same reason.

keyTerms.meaning: here too, the same applies in our case

steps.whatToRemember: An item that has the status of a כלי may be moved on שבת, even if it is restricted in other ways.

phrases.english: Here too,
phrases.notes: "Here" means the case רבא asked רב אויא about earlier.

phrases.english: since the status of a vessel applies to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי הוֹאִיל וְאִיכָּא תּוֹרַת כְּלִי עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies עולא's reason to the case at hand.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying a principle from a parallel case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: That the item in question might be מוקצה
steps.terutzMaskana: It may be moved because it has the status of a כלי

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק is glad רב אויא was not embarrassed
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק thanks God that רב אויא answered well and רבא did not embarrass him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Blessed is the Merciful One that רבא did not embarrass רב אויא.
steps.whatsHappening: This closes the story of רבא and רב אויא. רב נחמן בר יצחק is happy that רב אויא answered every question and was not put to shame.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא had pushed רב אויא with hard questions. רב אויא handled them all, ending with the proof from the jewelry. רב נחמן בר יצחק's blessing marks the end of the exchange.

keyTerms.meaning: blessed is the Merciful One, thank God
embarrassed him, put him to shame

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
Blessed is the Merciful One
that Rava did not embarrass Rav Avya.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּרִיךְ רַחֲמָנָא דְּלָא כַּסְּפֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב אַוְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the story after רב אויא's final answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב אויא answered רבא's questions successfully.

steps.title: אביי's first source: רבי שמעון allows leftover lamp oil
steps.stepSummary: אביי begins a contradiction before רבה. He quotes a ברייתא where the תנא קמא forbids leftover oil in a lamp or bowl, and רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי raised a contradiction to רבה. It was taught: The leftover oil in the lamp and in the bowl is forbidden, and רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion starts here. אביי is setting up a contradiction, and this is the first of his two sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Oil left over after a lamp burned on שבת is forbidden according to the first opinion. רבי שמעון permits it. This disagreement is the starting point for the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: raised a contradiction to him, set two sources against each other
the leftover oil
lamp
bowl

phrases.english: Abaye raised a contradiction to Rabba.
It was taught: the leftover oil
that is in the lamp and in the bowl
is forbidden, and Rabbi Shimon permits it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the רבא and רב אויא story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון permits leftover oil from a lamp burned on שבת.

steps.title: Conclusion from the first source: רבי שמעון does not hold of מוקצה
steps.stepSummary: From the oil ברייתא, אביי concludes that רבי שמעון does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Apparently, רבי שמעון does not hold of מוקצה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי draws a conclusion from the first source. Since רבי שמעון allows the oil, he must not hold of מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oil was set aside for burning when שבת began, yet רבי שמעון still allows it. So in his view, setting something aside does not make it forbidden. This conclusion is the side that the next source will clash with.

keyTerms.meaning: apparently, this shows that
something set aside and not meant for use on שבת, so it is forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי שמעון has no idea of מוקצה at all. Here we are only seeing that this kind of setting aside does not forbid the item in his view.

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לֵית לֵיהּ מוּקְצֶה.
phrases.english: Apparently, Rabbi Shimon does not hold of set-aside.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לֵית לֵיהּ מוּקְצֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a principle from the ברייתא in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי שמעון, there is no מוקצה prohibition (as seen from the oil case).

steps.title: The second source: רבי שמעון forbids what was not ready before יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes רבי שמעון from another source: a בכור whose blemish was not noticeable before יום טוב is not considered prepared. That sounds like רבי שמעון does hold of מוקצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they contradict it: רבי שמעון says: Any animal whose blemish was not noticeable from the eve of יום טוב is not among the prepared.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second half of אביי's contradiction. In another source, רבי שמעון forbids something that was not ready before יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the blemish only showed up on יום טוב, nobody could have planned before יום טוב to slaughter the animal. רבי שמעון forbids it because it was not prepared. Forbidding something for not being prepared is exactly the idea of מוקצה, so the two statements of רבי שמעון seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: and a contradiction is raised from another source
a blemish that disqualifies an animal from being a קרבן
the day before the festival
prepared, ready ahead of time for use

phrases.english: And they contradict it: Rabbi Shimon says:
Any animal whose blemish is not noticeable
phrases.notes: This is about a בכור animal that got a blemish. The גמרא expects you to know the case.

phrases.english: from the eve of the festival
is not among the prepared!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that clashes with the conclusion of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that רבי שמעון does not hold of מוקצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the בכור case, רבי שמעון forbids something because it was not prepared before יום טוב. That is a מוקצה-type rule, which contradicts his lenient ruling on the leftover oil.

steps.title: A lamp is expected to go out, a blemish is not
steps.stepSummary: רבה rejects the comparison. A person waits for his lamp to go out, but nobody sits and waits for a blemish to fall on his animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, a person sits and waits for his lamp to go out. Here, does a person sit and wait for a blemish to fall on his animal?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי's contradiction by showing that the two cases of רבי שמעון are really different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון does not have one rule that sometimes says מוקצה and sometimes not. What matters is whether the person expects the item to become usable. Leftover oil is fully expected, so the person never takes his mind off it. A blemish is not expected, so the animal is put out of mind.

keyTerms.meaning: 'How can you compare?' A way of rejecting a comparison between two cases.
Waits for and expects something to happen.
A blemish on an animal. A בכור may only be slaughtered once it has one.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that for רבי שמעון, the question is whether the person actually expects the item to become usable.

phrases.english: How can you compare these?
phrases.notes: רבה is speaking here, answering אביי's question from the previous step.

phrases.english: There, a person sits and waits
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case of the leftover oil in the lamp.

phrases.english: for when his lamp will go out.
Here, does a person sit and wait
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the case of the בכור.

phrases.english: for when a blemish will fall on it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: חילוק between the cases (distinguishing the cases)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי thought the oil case and the בכור case showed opposite opinions of רבי שמעון about מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both cases follow the same idea. Oil is expected to become free, so it is not מוקצה. A blemish is not expected, so the בכור is put out of mind.

steps.title: Three doubts about the firstborn animal
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains why the owner does not expect the בכור to become permitted. Maybe no blemish will come. Maybe it will not be permanent. Maybe no חכם will agree to examine it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He says: Who says a blemish will come? And even if it comes, who says it will be a permanent blemish? And even if it is permanent, who says a חכם will agree to deal with it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה continues his answer and spells out the owner's thinking: one doubt piled on another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each 'who says' adds another doubt. Only a מוּם קָבוּעַ that a חכם examines makes the בכור permitted. With so many doubts, the owner never really counts on it, so the animal is set aside in his mind.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Who says?' Raising a doubt about whether something will happen.
'Even if you say.' Granting one point and moving on to the next doubt.
A permanent blemish. Only this kind permits slaughtering a בכור.
Agrees to take on and deal with something.
A Sage who examines the blemish and rules on it.

steps.whatToRemember: Leftover oil is expected, so it is not מוקצה. A blemish on a בכור is far from certain, so the animal is put out of mind and becomes מוקצה.

phrases.english: He says:
phrases.notes: 'He' is the owner of the animal, thinking to himself.

phrases.english: Who says a blemish will fall on it?

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר דְּנָפֵיל בֵּיהּ מוּמָא —
phrases.english: And even if you say a blemish will fall on it,

phrases.aramaic: מִי יֵימַר דְּנָפֵיל בֵּיהּ מוּם קָבוּעַ.
phrases.english: who says a permanent blemish will fall on it?

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם תִּמְצֵי לוֹמַר דְּנָפֵל בֵּיהּ מוּם קָבוּעַ —
phrases.english: And even if you say a permanent blemish will fall on it,
who says a Sage will agree to deal with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵימָר אָמַר: מִי יֵימַר דְּנָפֵיל בֵּיהּ מוּמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out step 8's claim that nobody waits for a blemish.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the reason behind the distinction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the owner expects the בכור to become permitted, just as with the oil.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of three separate doubts, the owner puts the animal out of his mind.

steps.title: A source about vows on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא brings a משנה: a husband may nullify vows on שבת, and one may ask a חכם to release vows, when it is for the needs of שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא objected: One may nullify vows on שבת, and one may ask a חכם about vows, when it is for the needs of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא starts an objection to רבה by quoting a משנה. Here the גמרא is only setting up the attack, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Think of a woman who vowed that some food is forbidden to her. The משנה lets her husband cancel the vow on שבת so she can eat it that day. That suggests the food was never put out of mind, even though it depended on someone else agreeing to cancel the vow.

keyTerms.meaning: Nullifying vows. A husband can cancel certain vows of his wife.
Asking a חכם to release a person from his vow.
For the needs of שבת.

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama raised an objection:
One may nullify vows on Shabbat,
phrases.notes: This is a husband cancelling his wife's vow.

phrases.english: and one may ask a Sage about vows that are for the needs of Shabbat.
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to challenge רבה's last doubt in step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's point that an outcome depending on someone else agreeing ('who says a חכם will deal with it') makes the item מוקצה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה treats food that is free only if the husband agrees as usable on שבת. Here the source is quoted, and the next step applies it.

steps.title: Why not say the husband may refuse?
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא asks why the משנה allows it at all. Using רבה's logic, we should say, 'Who says the husband will agree to deal with it?', so the food should stay set aside.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why? Let us say: Who says the husband will agree to deal with her vow?
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא now aims the משנה straight at רבה's reasoning about a חכם agreeing to examine the blemish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman put the food out of mind when she made the vow, and it can only become free if her husband agrees to cancel it. That is the same kind of 'who says he will agree' doubt רבה used for the חכם. Yet the משנה lets her use the food on שבת, so that kind of doubt does not seem to make something מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And why?' Asking how a ruling can be correct.
'Let us say.' Suggesting a line of reasoning.
The husband, who has the power to nullify his wife's vows.

steps.confusionAlert: רמי בר חמא is not attacking the whole answer, only the last doubt, about someone else agreeing to act (the חכם or the husband).

phrases.english: And why should it be allowed?
phrases.notes: Why may she eat food she had put out of mind with her vow?

phrases.english: Let us say: Who says
that her husband will agree to deal with her vow?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? לֵימָא: מִי יֵימַר דְּמִיזְדְּקֵק לַהּ בַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the objection begun in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's third doubt: 'who says a חכם will agree to deal with it?'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a doubt about someone agreeing to act made things מוקצה, the vowed food should stay forbidden on שבת even after הפרה. The משנה permits it, so that doubt should not create מוקצה.

steps.title: A woman's vow depends on her husband from the start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the husband part of רמי בר חמא's question. Following רב פנחס in the name of רבא, every woman who vows does so on her husband's consent, so the food was never fully set aside.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it follows רב פנחס in the name of רבא, who said: every woman who makes a vow makes it on her husband's consent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers why a husband may cancel his wife's vow on שבת without the food being set aside. Her vow was tied to her husband's say from the very beginning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר חמא argued: who knows whether the husband will cancel the vow? So the food should be set aside, like the בכור. The answer is that a wife's vow is never a full, final vow. It always hangs on her husband's approval, so she never truly pushed the food out of her mind.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who makes a vow
Based on her husband's consent; dependent on his approval
A husband canceling his wife's vows

phrases.english: There, it follows רב פנחס in the name of רבא.
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case in the משנה about a husband canceling vows.

phrases.english: For רב פנחס said in the name of רבא:
Every woman who makes a vow
makes her vow on her husband's consent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the husband part of רמי בר חמא's challenge in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: a wife's vow is conditional from the outset.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the husband might not cancel the vow, the food should count as set aside, just like the בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: A wife's vow always depends on her husband, so the food was never fully set aside.

steps.title: But who says a חכם will agree to release the vow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises the second part of the question. The teaching allows asking about vows on שבת for שבת needs, but by רבה's logic, who says a חכם will agree to deal with it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: one may ask a חכם about vows needed for שבת, on שבת. Why? Let us say: who says a חכם will agree to deal with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now presses on the part of the teaching about asking a חכם. The answer about the husband does not cover this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 12 only works for a wife's vow. A person who vows for himself has no husband involved. He depends on finding a חכם willing to release him. That sounds just like רבה's reason for the בכור, so the food should be set aside here too.

keyTerms.meaning: Asking a חכם to release a vow
Something needed for שבת
Agrees to take up the matter, deals with it
A sage who can release vows

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One may ask a חכם to release vows
that are for the needs of שבת, on שבת.
And why? Let us say:
Who says a חכם will agree to deal with it?
phrases.notes: This is רבה's own reason from step 9, now turned against him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע נִשְׁאָלִין לִנְדָרִים שֶׁל צוֹרֶךְ הַשַּׁבָּת בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 12 answered only the husband case. This step presses on the חכם case, which that answer does not cover.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's reasoning that uncertainty about a חכם agreeing makes the item set aside.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Releasing a vow also depends on a חכם agreeing. Yet the teaching allows it, so the food is not treated as set aside. This contradicts רבה's logic.

steps.title: Vows have a backup, the בכור does not
steps.stepSummary: For a vow, if no חכם agrees, three ordinary people are enough to release it. For a בכור, there is no backup, so it is uncertain whether a חכם will deal with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, if a חכם does not agree, three ordinary people are enough for him. Here, who says a חכם will agree to deal with it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a vow can always be released, because three ordinary people can do it if no חכם agrees. A בכור has no such backup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With vows, the person is sure he will find a way to be released, so he never sets the food aside in his mind. With a בכור, only an expert חכם can judge the blemish, and he may refuse. So the owner really does give up on it, and רבה's distinction stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Three ordinary, non-expert people, who can release a vow
It is enough for him

steps.whatToRemember: רבה's rule: something counts as set aside when it is truly uncertain it will become permitted. A wife's vow (always tied to her husband) and a personal vow (three ordinary people can release it) are not truly uncertain. A בכור's blemish, which needs an expert חכם, is.

phrases.english: There,
phrases.notes: 'There' means vows; 'here' below means the בכור.

phrases.english: if a חכם does not agree to deal with it,
three ordinary people are enough for him.
Here,
who says a חכם will agree to deal with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם אִי לָא מִיזְדְּקֵק לֵיהּ חָכָם סַגְיָא לֵיהּ בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה הֶדְיוֹטוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13 by showing how vows differ from a בכור.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: vows have a guaranteed backup, the בכור does not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Releasing a vow is just as uncertain as getting a חכם to examine a בכור's blemish.
steps.terutzMaskana: Three ordinary people can release a vow, so it is never truly uncertain. Only the בכור needs a specific expert, so only there is the item set aside.

steps.title: Why does רבי שמעון forbid moving a burning lamp?
steps.stepSummary: אביי begins a contradiction. רבי שמעון allows moving a lamp only once it has gone out, and the reason seems to be a fear that moving a burning lamp could put it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי raised a contradiction to רב יוסף. Did רבי שמעון say that once the lamp has gone out, you may move it? That means: gone out, yes; still burning, no. Why not? Because maybe while he holds it, the flame will go out.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is setting up the first side of a contradiction. He reads רבי שמעון's rule about the lamp and works out the reason behind it. The second side comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון said a lamp may be moved after its flame has gone out. אביי reads this to mean a burning lamp may not be moved. The only reason he can find is the fear that moving it might put out the flame by accident.

keyTerms.meaning: It went out (the lamp's flame)
To move it (carrying or handling an object on שבת)
It goes out (the flame gets extinguished)

phrases.english: Abaye raised a contradiction to Rav Yosef:
Did Rabbi Shimon say
once it has gone out, it is permitted to move it?
Gone out: yes;
not gone out: no.
What is the reason?
Perhaps while he is holding it, it will go out?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of vows and רבה's logic has ended.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's rule that a lamp may be moved only after it has gone out
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: From the wording, a burning lamp is forbidden to move. The reason must be the fear of accidentally putting it out. This sets up a clash with his own rule about unintended acts.

steps.title: רבי שמעון permits unintended acts, like dragging furniture
steps.stepSummary: אביי finishes the contradiction. רבי שמעון holds that an unintended act is permitted, as a ברייתא shows: you may drag furniture even if it might make a furrow, as long as you don't mean to.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we know that רבי שמעון said an unintended act is permitted! As a ברייתא teaches: רבי שמעון says a person may drag a chair, bed, or bench, as long as he does not mean to make a furrow.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings the second side of his contradiction. רבי שמעון elsewhere allows something that might cause an accidental forbidden result, so why worry about the lamp going out?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dragging furniture might dig a groove in the ground, but רבי שמעון allows it because the person doesn't intend that. By the same logic, moving a burning lamp should be allowed, since the person doesn't intend to put out the flame. So the lamp rule and the furniture rule seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: An unintended act: a permitted action that might accidentally cause a forbidden result
Drags
A furrow or groove in the ground
A bench

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון does not say a furrow is fine. He says dragging is fine as long as you are not trying to make one. Everything depends on what the person intends.

phrases.english: But haven't we heard of Rabbi Shimon
that he said: an unintended act is permitted.
As it was taught in a baraita: Rabbi Shimon says:
A person may drag a chair, bed, and bench,
as long as he does not intend to make a furrow!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא שָׁמְעִינַן לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן דְּאָמַר דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּוֵּין מוּתָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contradiction begun in step 15 by bringing the clashing source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason given for forbidding the burning lamp (fear it might go out)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון permits unintended acts, as with dragging furniture. So an accidental putting-out of the flame should not be a reason to forbid moving the lamp.

steps.title: A Torah-level result is treated differently from a rabbinic one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון's leniency depends on how serious the act would be if done on purpose. Torah-level acts get a rabbinic decree even when unintended. Rabbinic-level acts are fully permitted when unintended.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wherever doing it on purpose would break a Torah law, רבי שמעון made a rabbinic decree against it even when it is not intended. Wherever doing it on purpose would only break a rabbinic law, רבי שמעון permits it when not intended, even from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves אביי's contradiction by splitting the two cases. Putting out a flame on purpose is a Torah prohibition. Making a furrow by dragging is only rabbinic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון's basic rule still holds: an unintended act is not a real violation. But when the possible result is a Torah-level מלאכה, like putting out a flame, he added a rabbinic decree to be careful. When the result would only be rabbinic, like this kind of furrow, no decree was needed, so dragging furniture is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition from the Torah itself
Made a decree: a protective rule added by the Sages
By rabbinic law
From the start: allowed even before the fact, not just accepted afterward

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי שמעון, an unintended act is permitted outright only when the possible result would be rabbinic if done on purpose. When the possible result is a Torah prohibition, he forbids it by rabbinic decree. That is why a burning lamp may not be moved, but furniture may be dragged.
steps.whyThisMatters: It refines רבי שמעון's well-known rule of דבר שאין מתכוין. The rule has a limit: how serious the possible result is changes whether he adds a decree.

phrases.english: Wherever, if he intends it,
there is a Torah prohibition,
phrases.notes: Like putting out the lamp's flame, which is a full Torah-level מלאכה.

phrases.english: when he does not intend it,
Rabbi Shimon made a rabbinic decree against it.
Wherever, if he intends it,
there is only a rabbinic prohibition,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is putting the furrow from dragging furniture in this group. It is only a rabbinic problem.

phrases.english: when he does not intend it,
Rabbi Shimon permits it, even from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הֵיכָא דְּכִי מִיכַּוֵין אִיכָּא אִיסּוּרָא דְאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 15 and 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק) by how serious the possible result is
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון's rule permitting unintended acts should apply equally to the lamp and to the furniture.
steps.terutzMaskana: Unintended acts whose result would be a Torah prohibition are forbidden by a rabbinic decree. Unintended acts whose result would only be rabbinic are fully permitted.

steps.title: רבא challenges with the clothing merchants
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a case about clothing merchants. There, an unintended act is fully permitted even though doing it on purpose would break a Torah law. This breaks the distinction from Step 17.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא objected: Clothing merchants may sell their garments the normal way, as long as they do not mean to use them against the sun when it is sunny or against the rain when it is rainy. The extra-careful people hang them on a stick behind their backs. Here, if he means to wear them, that is a Torah prohibition. Yet when he does not mean to, רבי שמעון permits it from the start!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a case that seems to contradict the answer from Step 17. In this case רבי שמעון allows an unintended act even though the act would be a Torah prohibition if done on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said that when the act would be Torah-level if done on purpose, רבי שמעון still forbids it by rabbinic decree. A merchant who wears כלאים garments on purpose to protect himself breaks a Torah law. Even so, he may carry them on his shoulders without any intention, with no decree at all, so the Step 17 distinction does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: Clothing or garments. Here it means garments of wool and linen mixed together (כִּלְאַיִם).
The modest or extra-careful people, who go beyond what is required.
They hang or sling something, here over a stick so it does not touch the body.

steps.confusionAlert: The merchant is not wearing the garments to get dressed. He is draping them on himself to display or carry them. The only problem would be if he meant to enjoy them as protection from sun or rain, which counts as wearing them.

phrases.english: Rava objected:
Clothing merchants may sell in their normal way,
phrases.notes: These are garments of wool and linen mixed together (כלאים). The merchant drapes them on himself while selling.

phrases.english: as long as he does not intend
in the sun, for protection from the sun,
or in the rain, for protection from the rain.
And the modest ones hang them on a stick behind them.
But here, where if he intends,
there is a Torah prohibition,
yet when he does not intend,
רבי שמעון permits it from the start!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The Step 17 distinction: רבי שמעון forbids unintended acts when the act would be Torah-level if done on purpose.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the clothing-merchant case, wearing the garments on purpose would be a Torah prohibition. Yet the unintended act is permitted from the start, so Torah-level seriousness does not lead רבי שמעון to forbid unintended acts.

steps.title: רבא introduces a new explanation
steps.stepSummary: The word אלא shows the Step 17 answer has been dropped. רבא is about to give a different reason why רבי שמעון forbids moving a burning lamp.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא drops the earlier answer and gets ready to give רבא's new explanation, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא means the earlier answer is being given up because of רבא's challenge. The question from Steps 15–16 is still open: why does רבי שמעון forbid moving a burning lamp? A new reason is about to be offered.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It shows that the earlier approach is dropped and a new one is coming.

steps.whatToRemember: The idea that רבי שמעון decrees against unintended Torah-level acts has fallen. The contradiction about the lamp needs a new answer.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of Step 18 and opens a new answer to the contradiction from Steps 15–16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the lamp ban came from a decree on unintended acts that would be Torah-level.
steps.terutzMaskana: That approach is dropped, and רבא will offer a different reason.
